literal: Celestial Phenomena Treatise, Part One
idiomatic: Celestial Phenomena Treatise I

literal: The Liao founded their state on You and Ying; rites, music, and institutions grew daily more complete, and for more than two hundred years they transmitted the calendar and issued the new moon.
idiomatic: The Liao rose from You and Ying; as ritual and institutions matured, they issued calendars and set the new moon for over two hundred years.

literal: Now, by imperial order we compile the History of Liao; its form resembles the Song and Jin histories, and the Great Brightness Calendar cannot be omitted.
idiomatic: Ordered to compile the History of Liao on the model of the Song and Jin histories, we cannot omit the Great Brightness Calendar.

literal: The calendrical methods were forbidden and unobtainable; seeking the epoch of the Great Brightness Calendar, we obtained Zu Chongzhi's methods in an external history.
idiomatic: Official calendrical methods were barred from circulation; in seeking the Great Brightness epoch we found Zu Chongzhi's procedures in an outside history.

literal: Were Chongzhi's methods what the Liao calendar derived from?
idiomatic: Did the Liao calendar ultimately derive from Chongzhi's methods?

literal: Our dynasty also once followed them.
idiomatic: The present dynasty too once adopted them.

literal: Calculating by Chongzhi's methods up to the year the Liao revised the calendar, and taking the epoch count from that, this is the Liao Great Brightness Calendar.
idiomatic: Working forward with Chongzhi's arithmetic to the Liao calendar reform and deriving the epoch from that point yields the Liao Great Brightness Calendar.

literal: The Liao calendar could indeed be supplemented on this basis, yet it is not supplemented; histories value lacunae in the text.
idiomatic: The Liao calendar could be reconstructed from this material, but we leave it unreconstructed, for histories prize deliberate gaps.

literal: The external history records its methods; the Directorate of Astronomy preserves its duties; for the History of Liao, this treatise suffices.
idiomatic: An outside history records the procedures, the Directorate of Astronomy keeps the office, and this treatise in the History of Liao is enough.

literal: Thus the Calendar and Celestial Phenomena Treatise was composed.
idiomatic: Hence the Calendar and Celestial Phenomena Treatise.

literal: In the sixth year of Emperor Wu of Song's Daming reign, Zu Chongzhi submitted the methods of the Jiazi Epoch Calendar, which had not yet been put into use; it was therefore named the Great Brightness Calendar.
idiomatic: In Song Daming year 6 (462 CE) Zu Chongzhi presented the Jiazi Epoch Calendar methods; before adoption they were called the Great Brightness Calendar.

literal: From the upper origin jiazi to the seventh year of Song Daming, guimao, is 51,939 years, outside the count.
idiomatic: From upper-origin jiazi to Song Daming year 7 (guimao) is 51,939 years beyond the epoch count.

literal: Procedure for computing new moons:
idiomatic: Procedure to compute new moons:

literal: Set in the upper-origin year count, outside the count; multiply by rule months; when full of rule years it makes accumulated months; what does not fill is intercalary remainder.
idiomatic: Take the years since upper origin (outside the count), multiply by rule months, divide by rule years for accumulated months; the remainder is intercalary remainder.

literal: When intercalary remainder is 247 or more, that year has an intercalation.
idiomatic: If intercalary remainder is 247 or above, the year has a leap month.

literal: Multiply accumulated months by the month factor; when full of the day factor it makes accumulated days; what does not fill is small remainder.
idiomatic: Multiply accumulated months by the month factor; divide by the day factor for accumulated days; the remainder is fractional day remainder (xiao yu).

literal: Remove six decades from accumulated days; what does not fill is greater remainder.
idiomatic: Subtract full sixty-day cycles from accumulated days; the remainder is greater remainder (da yu).

literal: Name greater remainder from jiazi, outside the count: that is the new moon of the eleventh month of the civil year sought.
idiomatic: Count greater remainder from jiazi (outside the count) to obtain the new moon of civil month 11 for the target year.

literal: When small remainder is 1,849 or more, that month is long (thirty days).
idiomatic: If fractional day remainder is 1,849 or more, the month is a long month (30 days).

literal: To seek the next month:
idiomatic: To find the next month:

literal: Add to greater remainder 29; to small remainder 2,090.
idiomatic: Add 29 to greater remainder and 2,090 to fractional day remainder.

literal: When small remainder fills the day factor, carry to greater remainder; when greater remainder fills six decades, remove it; name as before: the next month's new moon.
idiomatic: When fractional remainder fills the day factor, carry to greater remainder; when greater remainder fills sixty days, drop it and name as before for the next new moon.

literal: To seek first and full moon:
idiomatic: To find first quarter and full moon:

literal: Add to new-moon greater remainder 7; to small remainder 1,507; to small parts 1.
idiomatic: Add 7 to new-moon greater remainder, 1,507 to small remainder, and 1 to small parts.

literal: When small parts fill 4, carry to small remainder; when small remainder fills the day factor, carry to greater remainder; name as before: the first-quarter day.
idiomatic: When small parts reach 4, carry to small remainder; when small remainder fills the day factor, carry to greater remainder; name as before for first quarter.

literal: Add again to obtain full moon; add again for last quarter; add again for the next month's new moon.
idiomatic: Add again for full moon, again for last quarter, and again for the following new moon.

literal: Procedure for computing intercalation:
idiomatic: Procedure for computing intercalation:

literal: Subtract intercalary remainder from rule years; when the remainder fills the intercalation factor, obtain one month; name from the civil new year, outside the count: where the intercalation lies.
idiomatic: Subtract intercalary remainder from rule years; each time the remainder fills the intercalation factor you gain one month; count from civil new year (outside the count) to locate the leap month.

literal: Intercalations may advance or retreat; lack of a mid-climate is the standard.
idiomatic: Leap placement may shift; the rule is that a month without a mid-climate is intercalary.

literal: Procedure for computing the twenty-four qi:
idiomatic: Procedure to compute the twenty-four qi:

literal: Set in the upper-origin year count, outside the count; multiply by remainder number; when full of era factor it makes accumulated days; what does not fill is small remainder.
idiomatic: Take years since upper origin (outside the count), multiply by remainder number, divide by era factor for accumulated days; the remainder is fractional day remainder.

literal: Remove six decades from accumulated days; what does not fill is greater remainder.
idiomatic: Subtract sixty-day cycles from accumulated days; the remainder is greater remainder.

literal: Name greater remainder from jiazi, outside the count: the winter solstice day of the eleventh civil month.
idiomatic: Name greater remainder from jiazi (outside the count) for the winter solstice of civil month 11.

literal: To seek the next qi:
idiomatic: To find the next qi:

literal: Add to greater remainder 15; to small remainder 8,626; to small parts 5.
idiomatic: Add 15 to greater remainder, 8,626 to small remainder, and 5 to small parts.

literal: When small parts fill 6, carry to small remainder; when small remainder fills era factor, carry to greater remainder; name as before: the next qi day.
idiomatic: When small parts reach 6, carry to small remainder; when small remainder fills era factor, carry to greater remainder; name as before for the next qi.

literal: To seek the earth's kingly tenure:
idiomatic: To find the earth phase (tu wang) period:

literal: Add to winter-solstice greater remainder 27; to small remainder 15,528: the last month of winter when earth holds sway.
idiomatic: Add 27 to winter-solstice greater remainder and 15,528 to small remainder for the late-winter earth tenure day.

literal: Again add to greater remainder 91; to small remainder 12,270: the next earth tenure day.
idiomatic: Add again 91 to greater remainder and 12,270 to small remainder for the next earth tenure day.

literal: Procedure for computing submergence:
idiomatic: Procedure for computing submergence (mo):

literal: Multiply winter-solstice small remainder by 90; subtract from submergence parts; when full of submergence factor it makes days; what does not fill is day remainder; name the day from winter solstice, outside the count: the submergence day.
idiomatic: Multiply winter-solstice fractional remainder by 90, subtract from submergence parts; divide by submergence factor for days; the remainder is day remainder; count from winter solstice (outside the count) for the submergence day.

literal: To seek the next submergence:
idiomatic: To find the next submergence:

literal: Add days 69; day remainder 34,442; when remainder fills submergence factor, carry to days: the next submergence day.
idiomatic: Add 69 days and 34,442 to day remainder; when remainder fills submergence factor, carry to days for the next submergence.

literal: When day remainder is exhausted, it is extinguished.
idiomatic: When day remainder is exhausted, the cycle ends (mie).

literal: Procedure for the sun's lodge at each day:
idiomatic: Procedure for the sun's daily lodge:

literal: Multiply new-moon accumulated days by era factor to make degree dividend; remove circumference of heaven; when remainder fills era factor it makes accumulated degrees; what does not fill is degree remainder.
idiomatic: Multiply new-moon accumulated days by era factor for degree dividend; subtract circumference of heaven; quotient by era factor gives accumulated degrees; remainder is degree remainder.

literal: Name from Void I; remove lodges in sequence, outside the count: the sun's lodge at midnight on the eleventh-month new moon.
idiomatic: Name from lodge Void I, subtract successive lodges (outside the count) for the sun's lodge at midnight on month-11 new moon.

literal: To seek the next month:
idiomatic: To find the next month:

literal: Long month: add 30 degrees; short month: add 29 degrees; when entering Void, remove degree parts.
idiomatic: Add 30 degrees for a long month, 29 for a short month; when entering Void, subtract degree parts.

literal: To seek motion parts:
idiomatic: To find motion parts:

literal: Divide degree remainder by small-part factor; the obtained is motion parts; what does not fill is small parts; when small parts fill the factor, carry to motion parts; when motion parts fill the factor, carry to degrees.
idiomatic: Divide degree remainder by small-part factor for motion parts; the remainder is small parts; carry when parts fill their factors.

literal: To seek the next day: add one degree.
idiomatic: For the next day: add one degree.

literal: When entering Void, remove motion parts 6 and small parts 147.
idiomatic: On entering Void, subtract 6 motion parts and 147 small parts.

literal: Procedure for the moon's lodge at each time:
idiomatic: Procedure for the moon's lodge:

literal: Multiply new-moon small remainder by 124 to make degree remainder; again multiply new-moon small remainder by 860 for minute parts; when minute parts fill month factor, carry to degree remainder; when degree remainder fills era factor, it makes degrees.
idiomatic: Multiply new-moon fractional remainder by 124 for degree remainder and by 860 for minute parts; carry minute parts into degree remainder, then degree remainder into degrees by era factor.

literal: Subtract from the new-moon midnight solar lodge: then the moon's lodge.
idiomatic: Subtract this from the new-moon midnight solar position to obtain the moon's lodge.

literal: To seek the next month:
idiomatic: To find the next month:

literal: Long month: add 35 degrees, degree remainder 31,834, minute parts 77,967; short month: add 22 degrees, degree remainder 17,261, minute parts 62,736; when entering Void, remove degrees.
idiomatic: Long month: add 35 degrees plus the listed remainders and minute parts; short month: add 22 degrees plus its listed parts; on entering Void, subtract degrees.

literal: Procedure for entering the Slow-Fast sequence:
idiomatic: Procedure to enter the Slow-Fast sequence:

literal: Multiply new-moon accumulated days by communication factor to make communication dividend; remove communication cycle; when remainder fills communication factor it makes days; what does not fill is day remainder.
idiomatic: Multiply new-moon accumulated days by communication factor for communication dividend; subtract communication cycle; divide by communication factor for days; remainder is day remainder.

literal: Name the day, outside the count: the day entered in the sequence at midnight on the eleventh-month new moon.
idiomatic: Name the day (outside the count) for midnight entry into the sequence on month-11 new moon.

literal: To seek the next month:
idiomatic: To find the next month:

literal: Long month: add 2 days; short month: add 1 day; day remainder in each case 11,746.
idiomatic: Long month: add 2 days; short month: add 1 day; day remainder always 11,746.

literal: When the sequence fills 27 days and day remainder 14,631, then remove it.
idiomatic: When the sequence reaches 27 days with day remainder 14,631, drop that cycle.

literal: To seek the next day: add one day.
idiomatic: For the next day: add one day.

literal: To seek the sun's fixed lodge at each day:
idiomatic: To find the sun's true (fixed) daily lodge:

literal: Multiply midnight sequence-entry day remainder by decrease-increase rate; by decrease-increase, adjust the accumulated surplus-deficit parts; as difference rate to one; when obtained fills era factor it makes degrees; what does not fill is degree remainder; add surplus and subtract deficit from mean degree and remainder for fixed degree.
idiomatic: Multiply midnight sequence day remainder by the adjustment rate, apply surplus-deficit to accumulated parts, scale by difference rate; divide by era factor for degrees; add surplus or subtract deficit from mean solar degree for true position.

literal: When increasing fills the factor, or decreasing is insufficient, advance or retreat by era factor.
idiomatic: If increase overflows the factor or decrease underflows, adjust by one era factor.

literal: To seek degree motion parts, use the procedure above.
idiomatic: Find degree motion parts by the same method.

literal: To seek the next day, add according to the slow or fast entered.
idiomatic: For the next day, add according to whether the sequence entry is slow or fast.

literal: When entering Void, remove parts as in the procedure above.
idiomatic: On entering Void, subtract parts as above.
